findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in this reports bucket are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
The bucket sets no ACL and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so bucket/object ACLs or policies could expose report data publicly with no account-level guardrail.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to the report objects would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is disabled, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irreversibly (e.g., by ransomware or a compromised credential) with force_destroy also enabled.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest.
No server access logging is configured for this ledger bucket, so reads and writes to sensitive exports are not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be permanently destroyed or tampered with without recoverable prior versions.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so a future ACL or bucket policy change could silently make ledger data publicly readable.
The model artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server-side encryption configuration, so artifacts are stored unencrypted.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guarding this bucket against ACL- or policy-based public exposure.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set, so operational runbooks (which commonly contain internal hostnames, procedures, and secrets) are stored unencrypted.
No logging block is defined, so access to runbook content is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.
The bucket lacks an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, leaving no account-level guardrail against accidental public exposure.
The audit/log-delivery bucket itself has no access logging configured, so tampering with or exfiltration of audit logs is not independently recorded.
The audit log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a misconfigured ACL or policy could expose log data containing internal access patterns.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded into the unencrypted reports_archive bucket with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id specified, so potentially sensitive third-party data is stored in plaintext.
